warnings: op1 direct read (house 10). Completes the pile-footing detail series with S-08 (F3) — F4 and F6 shown here. Pile counts per mark (3/4/6) match the standard F<n>=n-piles convention noted in houses 07's diary entry, confirmed independently here.

NORMALIZED_2026-08-02: main_bar/stirrup were stored as free-text strings in this house (only houses 10 and 11 did this; the other 9 use nested objects). Converted to the schema section 6 object form. The exact original string is preserved verbatim in printed_as on every converted field, so nothing was lost and the parse can be re-checked against the drawing. 'Ø' was read as type RB per schema section 6. Thai annotations in parentheses (lap-splice/continuation notes) were carried into note. A 'tie'/'tie_bar' key was renamed to 'stirrup' to match the other houses. ⚠️ Bars printed with a mid-span/L-8 qualifier were NOT merged into a face count — that needs the section-7 leader-line check against the drawing image, which has not been done for this house yet.

NORMALIZED_2026-08-02: this house stored section data in per-file ad-hoc arrays (footing_types) instead of the elements[] that houses 01-09 use. Folded into elements[] with element_id/element_type, and mark->element_id, size_m -> width_mm/height_mm, thickness_m -> thickness_mm, rebar/top/bottom strings -> objects. Every original string is kept in a *_printed_as field. NOTE: the array named 'column_sections' actually held BEAM sections - every cut_ref names a B-mark - so those became element_type 'beam', with the cut label kept in section_ref. confidence_score is null because this house never recorded one; it was NOT invented.
